observations.observation: Header bar color differs. The original has a solid red header bar (rgb(210,60,51), about 100px tall). The AI-built page has a dark header bar about 64px tall. Both put the logo on the left and a single row of nav links on the right.

tags.value: changed: tall red bar becomes slim dark bar

observations.observation: The logo is the same 83×59 Logo.gif on both pages but at different sizes. The original shows it at 80×57 with no brand text beside it. The AI-built page shrinks it to 40×28 and adds a text brand link next to it.

tags.value: changed: large logo becomes small logo with text brand

observations.observation: Nav links differ. The original's nav has dropdown carets (About Us, Flying with Us) and FontAwesome icons before Contact Us, Flight Schedule and the phone number. The AI-built nav has six plain cream sans text links with no icons, dropdowns, underline or active state.

tags.value: changed: nav with carets and icons becomes plain text links
changed: dropdown carets on nav items

observations.observation: Both heroes are a full-width dark band with a photograph of a carved Alaska Native owl mask behind the text.

tags.value: kept: full-width dark band with owl mask photo

observations.observation: Hero size and content differ. The original hero is about 800px tall, and the h1 and a white flight-search card sit directly over the photo. The AI-built hero is 486px tall: a left-aligned column about 626px wide holds an eyebrow, h1, serif lead paragraph and two CTAs. The photo subject sits to the right and is not overlapped, and the search form moves to its own section below.

tags.value: changed: tall photo with search card becomes shorter left-text hero

observations.observation: The h1 differs. The original is two uppercase lines, 'GRANT AVIATION' in white and 'ALASKAN-OWNED AND OPERATED' in red, at 48px Raleway weight 400. The AI-built h1 is 'Fly Easy, Fly Grant.' at 64px bold Helvetica Neue in cream (rgb(244,236,220)). Its 'owned and operated by Alaskans' line becomes a small eyebrow instead. Both pages have exactly one h1.

tags.value: changed: uppercase two-line h1 becomes bold cream sentence-case h1

observations.observation: The AI-built page opens every section with a small uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow label above a 32px bold h2. Eyebrows are rust on light sections, peach on the dark section and orange-tan in the hero. The original has no eyebrow labels.

tags.value: added: uppercase letterspaced eyebrow above headings

observations.observation: The original's welcome heading is uppercase, light-weight and white, with a short red rule beneath it as an accent.

tags.value: dropped: short red rule under welcome heading

observations.observation: The AI-built hero has two CTAs side by side: a filled rust 'Book a flight' button and an outlined 'Flight schedule & status' button with a white border. The original hero has no CTA buttons, only the search card.

tags.value: added: filled and outline hero buttons

observations.observation: Primary button styling differs. The original's 'Search for flights' button is a flat red rectangle with square (0px) corners that fills about half the card width. The AI-built buttons are rust (rgb(168,52,31)) with white text, a 6px radius and 12px × 22.4px padding.

tags.value: changed: flat square red button becomes rounded rust button
changed: square corners become small rounding

observations.observation: The search card is white on both pages, but treated differently. The original card is about 808px wide, sits over the hero left of centre and has no visible shadow. The AI-built card is a 1080px form in its own section, with a 1px border, rounded corners and the page's only box shadow.

tags.value: changed: search card over hero becomes own section bordered card with shadow

observations.observation: Both search forms have a Return/One way radio pair, origin and destination fields, departure and return dates, and Adults/Children/Infants counts.

tags.value: kept: same flight search fields

observations.observation: Passenger inputs differ. The original uses Bootstrap-style steppers with −/+ buttons either side of a centred number, in three columns. The AI-built page uses native selects and native mm/dd/yyyy date inputs. Its 5-column first row leaves Children and Infants alone on the second row, with the right two-thirds empty.

tags.value: changed: stepper inputs become native selects and date inputs

observations.observation: Form heading and labels differ. The original heading is 'Search for Flights', a 30px weight-400 h2, with small grey regular-weight labels. The AI-built heading is 'Where are you headed?', a 32px bold h2, with small bold sans labels and serif placeholders ('e.g. Anchorage').

tags.value: changed: light heading and grey labels become bold heading and bold labels

observations.observation: In the original form, the 'Traveling to' label is greyed out because its field is disabled.

tags.value: dropped: greyed disabled field label

observations.observation: The agent link differs. The original puts a small grey right-aligned 'Agent Login »' link next to the search button. The AI-built page puts an inline sentence beside the button: 'Travel agent login · Reserve by phone: 888-Fly-Grant (888-359-4726)'.

tags.value: changed: agent login link becomes inline sentence with phone

observations.observation: The palettes differ. The original is red (rgb(210,60,51)), dark charcoal (rgb(34,34,34) on 61 elements), blue-grey slate and white. The AI-built page is warm: a cream page background (rgb(251,247,239)), near-black bands (rgb(11,10,12)) and one rust accent (rgb(168,52,31)). Both use a single red-family accent on buttons, links and highlights.

tags.value: changed: red charcoal and slate becomes cream near-black and rust

observations.observation: Body text differs. The original sets it in mid-grey rgb(114,114,114) at 16px/24px on white, with rgb(51,51,51) for headings. The AI-built page sets it in near-black rgb(29,26,23) at 17px/27.2px on cream, with rgb(95,88,80) as secondary text.

tags.attribute: body text size and line height
tags.value: changed: 16px 1.5 becomes 17px 1.6
changed: mid-grey body text becomes near-black with grey meta

observations.observation: Type families differ. The original uses Open Sans for nearly all text (568 elements), Raleway for the h1 and some headings, and FontAwesome for icons. The AI-built page uses Georgia serif for body, lists and inputs (127 elements) and Helvetica Neue/Arial sans for headings, nav, buttons and labels.

tags.value: changed: open sans and raleway become georgia and helvetica

observations.observation: Secondary navigation differs. The original has a white grid of 8 icon-link tiles (4×2) with red FontAwesome glyphs, small labels and hairline dividers, beside a dark slate text panel. The AI-built page has a 'More ways to fly' section of 5 white bordered, rounded text cards (3 + 2, leaving one empty cell). Each card has an h3, a grey serif blurb and a rust link ending in '→'.

tags.value: changed: icon tile grid becomes bordered text cards

observations.observation: AI-built cards stretch to the tallest card in each row (253px in the first row). Short blurbs leave empty space under the link.

tags.value: added: fixed height cards with empty space

observations.observation: The COVID-19 notice is treated differently. In the original it is a long bold white justified paragraph with black highlight bars behind each line, inside the dark slate welcome panel. The AI-built page puts a full-width tan aside band (rgb(233,223,200)) with a bold 'COVID-19 update:' lead-in and an underlined link under the hero. It then repeats the topic as a bulleted list of rules in the Welcome section's right column.

tags.value: changed: highlighted paragraph becomes tan band and list

observations.observation: Both welcome areas have columns of very different heights. In the original, the dark slate panel is much taller than the tile grid, leaving a blank dark area to the right. In the AI-built page, the left text column (54px paragraph) is much shorter than the right COVID list (272px).

tags.value: changed: panel and tiles become uneven two-column welcome

observations.observation: Page width is handled differently. The original uses a boxed container (about x=105–1335) with shadows on its left and right edges, and dark bands visible behind it. The AI-built page holds content to a 1080px column starting at x=180, with full-bleed section backgrounds and no edge shadows.

tags.value: changed: boxed shadowed container becomes centered 1080px column in full-bleed bands

observations.observation: The original has an 'Alaska Charter Flights' text column with a 'Keep reading…' red link. Below it, an embedded video iframe shows only a black rectangle with a play button and no poster. The AI-built page reduces charters to one card and has no video.

tags.value: dropped: charter text with empty video embed

observations.observation: Destinations differ. The original shows a plain 2-column list of 8 towns with red map-pin icons, on white beside the charter column. The AI-built page shows the same 8 towns as outlined bold sans tiles on a 5-column grid, inside a near-black band with cream text and a peach 'More about destinations →' link.

tags.value: changed: pin icon list becomes outlined tile grid on dark band

observations.observation: The original has a pale blue-grey reservation band. It centres 'Make a Reservation Today!' over a very large red '888-Fly-Grant' (about 56px), with a faint plane silhouette and a red 'Book online' button.

tags.value: dropped: large phone number reservation band

observations.observation: Social content differs. The original has a 'Lets get Social' heading with an empty area under it, where an embedded widget appears not to have loaded. The AI-built page has only a text line: 'Follow us on Facebook and Twitter.'

tags.value: changed: empty social widget becomes text line

observations.observation: News differs. The original has a single bordered card with an uppercase 'GRANT AVIATION SUMMER NEWSLETTER 2018' title and a clock icon. Its body is a raw red PDF URL that overflows and is clipped. The AI-built page has a bordered list of two dated entries (2018 and 2016) using <time> elements, bold sans h3 titles and serif links separated by '·'.

tags.value: changed: single card becomes bordered list of dated entries

observations.observation: The original contains a 'shp.png' image (natural 1090×457) stretched to 1338×561 at y=1142, with empty alt text and no matching visible content.

tags.value: dropped: stretched decorative image

observations.observation: Newsletter sign-up differs. In the original it is a red inline 'Sign up here' text link in the footer, with no input. In the AI-built page it is a rust button-styled <a> ('Sign up to our newsletter') in its own column beside News. That column ends well above the news column.

tags.value: changed: footer text link becomes rust button link

observations.observation: The AI-built page has a Careers section: an h2 and one short paragraph about 680px wide, with no link and empty space to the right.

tags.value: added: careers section with short paragraph

observations.observation: Contact details are presented differently. The original lists them in the footer with red envelope and headset icons and white text. The AI-built page uses a description list in its own Contact section: grey bold sans terms (Phone, Facebook, Twitter, Website, Online) beside underlined serif links.

tags.value: changed: footer icon lines become dl contact section

observations.observation: Footer structure differs. The original is a tall dark slate footer with four uppercase columns (Legal, Follow Us, Contact Us, Quick Links), a Photos strip and a Newsletter block. Under that sits a near-black bottom bar with a 'Staff Login' link. The AI-built footer is a slim 104px dark band with a copyright line on the left and four underlined cream links on the right.

tags.value: changed: tall four-column footer becomes slim band with links

observations.observation: Original footer links use small grey square icon chips with red glyphs (Facebook, Twitter, plane, calendar, paper plane).

tags.value: dropped: footer icon chips

observations.observation: The original footer has a row of six low-resolution photo thumbnails (76×67 shown at 67×59) with white frames, plus a red 'More photos' button. The AI-built page has only a 'More photos' text link.

tags.value: dropped: footer photo thumbnails

observations.observation: Both pages show a copyright line for 2015–2021 Grant Aviation. In the original, the brand name is red.

tags.value: kept: copyright line

observations.observation: Image use differs. The original has 9 images, with alt text auto-generated from camera filenames (e.g. 'IMG_0548.jpg') and some empty alts. The AI-built page has 1 image (the logo, empty alt), with the hero as a CSS background. Neither page has a missing alt attribute.

tags.value: changed: many photos become single css background
changed: filename alts become empty alt

observations.observation: Section backgrounds differ. The original sequence is dark hero photo, dark slate welcome band, white charter area, pale blue-grey reservation band, white social/news area and dark slate footer. The AI-built page alternates through dark hero, tan notice, cream, white, cream-tint, black destinations, cream, white, cream and black footer, with hairline borders between light bands.

tags.value: changed: slate and white bands become alternating cream white and dark bands

observations.observation: The AI-built page has regular vertical rhythm. Each section has about 64px of top padding before the eyebrow, and the h2 sits about 29px below it in every section.

tags.value: added: regular gutters and section padding

observations.observation: Link styling differs. Original links are red Open Sans text (e.g. 'Keep reading…'), often paired with FontAwesome icons. AI-built links are underlined rust serif text with trailing '→' and '·' separators.

tags.value: changed: red links become underlined rust links
changed: icon links become text arrow links

observations.observation: Icons differ. The original uses the FontAwesome icon font (32 elements) for nav, tiles, pins and footer chips. The AI-built page has no icons and uses text arrows. Neither page has any SVG elements.

tags.value: changed: icon fonts become text glyphs

observations.observation: Layout technique differs. The original uses float and legacy grid with no CSS grid or flexbox (display_grid 0, display_flex 0). The AI-built page uses CSS grid (6) and flexbox (10).

tags.value: changed: floats become flex plus grid

observations.observation: Class usage differs. The original has a Bootstrap-like vocabulary of 598 classes (153 unique). The AI-built page has 58 classes (22 unique). Neither is utility-based (tailwind_like_fraction 0.015 vs 0.017).

tags.value: changed: many class names become few custom classes

observations.observation: Semantic markup differs. The original is div- and span-heavy, with 1 header, 1 nav, 1 section, 1 footer and no main or aside. The AI-built page has a header, nav, main, aside, 7 sections and a footer. Neither has article or figure elements.

tags.value: changed: divs become header nav main sections

observations.observation: Heading structure differs. The original mixes 5 h2, 10 h3 and 15 h5 elements in an inconsistent order. The AI-built page follows h1 → 8 h2 sections → 8 h3 items with no skipped levels.

tags.value: changed: flat irregular outline becomes structured h1 h2 h3

observations.observation: Asset weight differs. The original loads 34 scripts and 18 stylesheets and has 25 inline style attributes. The AI-built page has 1 script, no external stylesheets, a single inline <style> block and 13 inline style attributes.

tags.value: changed: many scripts and stylesheets become single inline style

observations.observation: Form and ARIA markup differ. The original has 125 ARIA attributes, 61 option elements, 2 hidden selects and 9 buttons. The AI-built page has 3 ARIA attributes, 23 options, 3 selects and 1 real button, with CTAs made from styled anchors.

tags.value: changed: heavy aria becomes minimal aria
changed: styled anchors rather than button elements

observations.observation: Both pages use mostly square corners. The original has almost no rounding (632 elements at 0px, 7 small, 2 pill). The AI-built page uses 6–12px radii on its cards, form and buttons (20 small, 6 medium, no pills).

tags.value: changed: square corners become small rounding

observations.observation: Decorative effects differ. The original has 4 gradients, 9 box shadows, 58 transitions and 29 transforms. The AI-built page has no gradients, transitions or transforms and 1 shadow. Neither page uses animations or backdrop blur.

tags.value: changed: shadows gradients transitions become flat with one shadow

observations.observation: Both pages use plain copy with an Alaskan regional flavour: 'Quyana Rewards', named Alaska communities and the '888-Fly-Grant' mnemonic. The AI-built page adds the tagline 'Fly Easy, Fly Grant.' and a question-style heading.

tags.value: kept: plain regional copy with mnemonic phone number

observations.observation: Both pages have short copy (481 vs 511 words) with no emoji and no em dashes, and 2 vs 1 exclamation marks.

tags.value: kept: no emoji or em dashes

observations.observation: Both pages contain dated content: COVID-19 travel messaging, news from 2018 (Jun 12, 2018) and a 2015–2021 copyright.

tags.value: kept: same dated items and copyright notice

observations.observation: The AI-built page uses British spelling ('Our loyalty programme') in the Quyana Rewards blurb.

tags.value: added: british spelling in rewards blurb

observations.observation: Capitalisation differs. The original mixes cases: all-caps radios ('RETURN TRIP'), uppercase welcome, news and footer headings, and title case in the nav. The AI-built page keeps uppercase to eyebrow labels and sets headings in sentence case.

tags.value: changed: all-caps headings become sentence case headings
